quests.question: A
quests.hint: Start with two slanted lines that meet at the top, then add a small line across the middle.
quests.funFact: The letter A is the most commonly used first letter in the English alphabet.

quests.question: B
quests.hint: Draw a straight line down, then add two round bumps on the right side.
quests.funFact: B comes from the Phoenician letter 'beth', which means house.

quests.question: C
quests.hint: Start near the top and curve all the way around, like a smile that doesn't close.
quests.funFact: The letter C is the 12th most frequently used letter in the English language.

quests.question: D
quests.hint: Draw a straight line down, then add one big curve on the right side.
quests.explanation: Fantastic! You practiced the letter 'D' beautifully!
quests.funFact: D is the mathematical Roman numeral for 500.

quests.question: E
quests.hint: Draw a straight line down, then add three short lines going right.
quests.explanation: Amazing! The letter 'E' is written neatly!
quests.funFact: E is the most commonly used letter in the English language.

quests.question: F
quests.hint: Draw a straight line down, then add two short lines going right at the top.
quests.funFact: F was originally called 'digamma' in early Greek.

quests.question: G
quests.hint: Curve around like a 'C', then add a small line going in near the bottom.
quests.funFact: G was added to the Latin alphabet to distinguish its sound from C.

quests.question: H
quests.hint: Draw two straight lines down, then join them with a line across the middle.
quests.explanation: Nicely done! 'H' is complete and looking sharp!
quests.funFact: H is the most common consonant to be silent in English.

quests.question: I
quests.hint: Draw one straight line from the top to the bottom.
quests.funFact: The dot over a lowercase 'i' is called a tittle.

quests.question: J
quests.hint: Draw a line down, then curve it to the left at the bottom.
quests.funFact: J is the only letter that doesn't appear on the periodic table of elements.

quests.question: K
quests.hint: Draw a straight line down, then add two slanted lines that meet in the middle.
quests.funFact: K comes from the Greek letter Kappa.

quests.question: L
quests.hint: Draw a straight line down, then add a short line along the bottom.
quests.explanation: Well done! 'L' is written so clearly!
quests.funFact: L is the 11th most frequently used letter in the English language.

quests.question: M
quests.hint: Draw two straight lines down, then connect them with a 'V' in the middle.
quests.explanation: Good job! You wrote the letter 'M' with care!
quests.funFact: M often symbolizes 'thousand', from the Roman numeral system.

quests.question: N
quests.hint: Draw two straight lines down, then join them with one slanted line.
quests.funFact: N is the 6th most common letter in the English alphabet.

quests.question: O
quests.hint: Draw one smooth curve all the way around, like a circle.
quests.funFact: O is the oldest letter in the alphabet, unchanged since 1300 BC.

quests.question: P
quests.hint: Draw a straight line down, then add a round bump at the top.
quests.funFact: The letter P makes up about 2% of the letters used in English.

quests.question: Q
quests.hint: Draw a circle like an 'O', then add a small tail at the bottom.
quests.explanation: Fantastic! You practiced the letter 'Q' beautifully!
quests.funFact: Q is almost always followed by the letter U in English words.

quests.question: R
quests.hint: Draw a straight line down, add a bump at the top, then a slanted leg.
quests.explanation: Amazing! The letter 'R' is written neatly!
quests.funFact: R is known as the 'littera canina' or canine letter because its trill sounds like a dog snarling.

quests.question: S
quests.hint: Curve to the left at the top, then curve the other way at the bottom.
quests.funFact: More English words begin with the letter S than any other letter.

quests.question: T
quests.hint: Draw a line across the top, then a straight line down the middle.
quests.funFact: T is the most common consonant in the English language.

quests.question: U
quests.hint: Draw a curve like a smile, then bring both ends straight up.
quests.explanation: Nicely done! 'U' is complete and looking sharp!
quests.funFact: U and V were considered the same letter until the 16th century.

quests.question: V
quests.hint: Draw two slanted lines that meet at the bottom, like a checkmark.
quests.funFact: V is the only letter in English that is never silent.

quests.question: W
quests.hint: Draw two 'V' shapes side by side.
quests.funFact: W is the only English letter whose name has more than one syllable.

quests.question: X
quests.hint: Draw two slanted lines that cross in the middle.
quests.funFact: X is the least used letter in the English language.

quests.question: Y
quests.hint: Draw two slanted lines that meet in the middle, then one line straight down.
quests.explanation: Well done! 'Y' is written so clearly!
quests.funFact: Y is sometimes a vowel and sometimes a consonant.

quests.question: Z
quests.hint: Draw a line across the top, a slanted line down, then a line across the bottom.
quests.explanation: Good job! You wrote the letter 'Z' with care!
quests.funFact: Z is the least frequently used letter in written English.

quests.hint: Draw one smooth curve all the way around, like an egg shape.
quests.funFact: The concept of zero was invented in ancient India.

quests.hint: Draw one straight line from the top to the bottom.
quests.funFact: One is the only number that is neither prime nor composite.

quests.hint: Curve at the top, slant down, then draw a straight line along the bottom.
quests.funFact: Two is the only even prime number.

quests.hint: Draw two curves stacked on the right side, like two little bumps.
quests.explanation: Fantastic! You practiced the number '3' beautifully!
quests.funFact: Three is the first odd prime number.
